gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a NAS costs to run when it sits idle 23 hours a day and backs up for one. From the makers' own power figures, a nightly 1-hour backup plus 23 hours of drive sleep costs about $10/yr on a Synology DS225+ and about $30/yr on a QNAP TS-264 at the US average rate. The TS-264 draws 18.3 W even with its disks in standby, against 6.1 W for the DS225+.
standout_why: I opened the two Synology pages ChatGPT cited, the Active Backup for Business spec (DSM 7.4) and the Snapshot Replication spec (DSM 7.4). Both give software limits only: concurrent backups by RAM, snapshot counts, free-space minimums. Neither has any wattage or running cost. ChatGPT's answer and our current page's columns (CPU, backup route, snapshots, warranty) also have no power or energy figure. For a box that works about one hour a night, the idle draw is most of its running cost, and no rival page states it.
decides: It backs the Synology DS225+ (or DS425+) over the QNAP TS-264 for this low-duty job. The QNAP's 'Disk Standby' draw is about 3× Synology's hibernation draw, so it costs about $19 more per year and about $58 more over its 3-year warranty. That is a tiebreaker, not the deciding factor. The UGREEN DXP2800 comes out cheapest to run at about $9/yr, but its figures come from a reviewer's spec list rather than the maker's page. I could not source current enclosure prices today, so this covers running cost only, not total cost of ownership.
